title: [IELTS INSIGHTS JAN 26] - Daily oil production in 4 countries: 2000 - 2004
prompt: The table below shows daily oil production in 4 countries from 2000 to 2004. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table gives information about the amount of oil produced by four countries, namely Nigeria, Chad, Congo and Somalia, between 2000 and 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, with the exception of Congo, all the remaining countries expanded their production towards the end of the period. Nigeria and Congo were by far the largest producers, whereas Chad, despite showing the most substantial increases, produced the smallest amount of oil.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking first at the leading oil producers, in 2000, 205,000 barrels of oil were produced by Nigeria daily, which was significantly lower than Congo's production, at 275,000 barrels. Thereafter, continuous declines were recorded in the latter country, and in 2004, its figure was 203,000 barrels per day. In contrast, Nigeria's production decreased to 190,000 barrels in 2002, but then rebounded to 213,000 at the end of the period, allowing this country to surpass Congo as the largest oil producer.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to the two smaller producers, which both saw dramatic growth, Somalia produced only an average of 5,000 barrels a day in the first year, while Chad recorded no production for the first three years. After that, Chad started to produce 8,000 barrels per day in 2003, before dramatically increasing its production to 50,000 barrels daily in 2004, which represented the highest annual growth. Somalia, meanwhile, experienced drastic increases in its oil production, reaching the same figure as Chad in the final year.
